findings.detail: AC#3 requires the realpath()/abspath() family to be 'split to a linked follow-up ticket.' The ticket's deps (from show_ticket snapshot) contain only two related tickets — 2305-0d04-0cfd-441a and 8a87-6c9b-6861-4ac3 — both are code-review artifacts for the same Gerrit change, not a separate follow-up design-judgment ticket. The per-site design decisions are documented inline in this ticket's body and RCA comment, but no separate linked follow-up ticket is visible in the deps snapshot I read. The realpath(tracker) sites remain in the codebase (reads.py:238, reads.py:244, compact_txn.py:523, compact_rebuild.py:138, compact_plan.py:211, fsck.py:252, fsck_tracker_health.py:82/203/373, _proc.py:141) without a linked follow-up ticket to own their resolution.
findings.remediation: Create a follow-up ticket for the realpath()/abspath() design-judgment family (reads.py:238/:249/:374, compact_txn.py:523, compact_rebuild.py:138, compact_plan.py:211, fsck.py:252, fsck_tracker_health.py:82/203/373, _proc.py:141) and link it to this ticket with a `discovered_from` or `relates_to` dep. Record the per-site design decisions (store-repo sanction vs. threading repo_root) in that ticket's description. Then record the follow-up ticket id as a comment on this ticket.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
